text_summary: During morning shift changeover at BAY-2, welding operations under permit P-2291 were conducted 8 metres from pressure vessel V-204B. H2S readings at the vessel neck climbed from 4 ppm to 28 ppm over 12 minutes while incoming shift personnel had not yet assumed gas-watch responsibilities. The area was evacuated when a portable monitor alarmed at 25 ppm; post-incident analysis attributed the release to a micro-leak at the V-204B upper flange gasket that had been flagged for replacement three weeks earlier.

Pressure relief valve PRV-101 on vessel V-101A failed to reseat after a routine over-pressure event, venting process gas for approximately 45 minutes before an operator noticed the continuous discharge sound. The B-shift operator had been on a 14-hour extended shift due to staffing shortage. No injuries occurred, but the delayed response extended the venting duration and required a controlled depressurisation of V-101A.

Reciprocating compressor C-14 experienced a primary seal failure at the drive-end bearing housing following three days of gradually increasing vibration readings that exceeded the 12 mm/s alarm threshold. Process gas migrated through the failed seal into the compressor enclosure, triggering LEL detectors at 35% LEL. Emergency shutdown was initiated automatically, and the gas cloud dispersed within 20 minutes under favourable wind conditions.

Heat exchanger HX-110 shell-side outlet temperature exceeded its 285°C design limit by 18°C after progressive tube-side fouling reduced heat transfer efficiency over a six-week period. The temperature excursion triggered the high-temperature alarm but not the trip. Operations manually reduced feed rate and brought the exchanger offline for cleaning. Inspection revealed heavy coke deposits on 40% of the tube bundle.

Storage tank T-301 reached 97% capacity during a naphtha transfer when the primary level transmitter LT-301A read 82% due to zero-point drift. The independent high-level switch had been bypassed under a maintenance override tag from two days prior that had not been cleared. A field operator on routine rounds noticed the rising liquid level through the sight glass and halted the transfer 14 minutes before projected overflow into the bund.

A flange leak developed on pressure vessel V-302A during hot work grinding operations on an adjacent piping spool in BAY-3. The isolation plan for the grinding work did not include V-302A's downstream connections, and a residual hydrocarbon vapour pocket ignited briefly at the leak point. The flash fire was extinguished by the fire watch within 8 seconds. Investigation found that the isolation boundary had been drawn one flange joint too narrow, and the V-302A gasket was original equipment from the 2018 installation.

Reactor R-501 experienced an uncontrolled exothermic excursion when the primary cooling water loop tripped on low flow and the standby pump failed to auto-start due to a seized impeller. Reactor bed temperature rose from 340°C to 520°C in 9 minutes. The emergency quench system was activated manually after a 4-minute delay because the control room operator initially misread the temperature trend as a sensor fault. The pressure excursion ruptured a reactor nozzle weld, releasing hot process gas that fatally injured one field technician in the adjacent pipe rack.

Centrifugal pump PP-205 developed a visible hydrocarbon spray from the outboard mechanical seal while transferring light cycle oil at 12 bar. The spray was directed toward a cable tray but did not reach any ignition source. Investigation found that the seal had exceeded its 18-month replacement interval by 5 months, and a 3/4-inch drain valve on the seal flush line had been left in the open position after a maintenance check, reducing seal flush pressure below the minimum 2 bar threshold.
